"'''Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast'''" is a song written by [[Peter Callander]] and [[Geoff Stephens]] and performed by [[Wayne Newton]]. It appeared on Newton's 1972 album, ''Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.discogs.com/Wayne-Newton-Daddy-Dont-You-Walk-So-Fast/release/1949515 |title=Wayne Newton - Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast (Vinyl, LP, Album) |website=Discogs.com |year=1972 |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref> In the lyrics, the singer is leaving his family after falling out of love with his wife. When his daughter tries to catch up with him, saying "Daddy, don't you walk so fast", it makes him change his mind about ending his marriage.<ref>[https://genius.com/Wayne-newton-daddy-dont-you-walk-so-fast-lyrics Genius.com "Wayne Newton--Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast". Retrieved March 7, 2025]</ref>

"Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast" reached No. 3 on the U.S. [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|adult contemporary chart]] and No. 4 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicvf.com/song.php?title=Daddy%2C+Don%27t+You+Walk+So+Fast+by+Wayne+Newton&id=48466 |title=Daddy, Don't You Walk So Fast (song by Wayne Newton) |website=Musicvf.com |date=1972-04-22 |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref> The song spent one week at No. 1 on the [[Cashbox (magazine)|''Cashbox'' chart]] on August 5, 1972,<ref name="tropicalglen.com">{{cite web|url=http://tropicalglen.com/Archives/70s_files/19720805.html|title=Cash Box Top 100 8/05/72|website=Tropicalglen.com|accessdate=19 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180627230922/http://tropicalglen.com/Archives/70s_files/19720805.html|archive-date=27 June 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and three weeks at No. 1 in Australia. It sold over one million copies and was awarded a [[music recording sales certification|gold disc]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] in July 1972.<ref name="The Book of Golden Discs">{{cite book | first= Joseph | last= Murrells | year= 1978 | title= The Book of Golden Discs | edition= 2nd | publisher= Barrie and Jenkins Ltd | location= London | page= [https://archive.org/details/bookofgoldendisc00murr/page/317 317] | isbn= 0-214-20512-6 | url-access= registration | url= https://archive.org/details/bookofgoldendisc00murr/page/317 }}</ref>

The song was ranked No. 10 on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine's Top [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] songs of 1972<ref>{{cite web|url=http://longboredsurfer.com/charts/1972.php |title=Charts:1972  |accessdate=January 16, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216000410/http://longboredsurfer.com/charts/1972.php |archivedate=February 16, 2016 }}</ref> and was also ranked No. 7 on the [[Kent Music Report]]'s 25 songs of 1972.

The track was produced by [[Wes Farrell]] and arranged by [[Mike Melvoin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.45cat.com/record/780100 |title=Wayne Newton - Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast / Echo Valley 2-6809 - Chelsea - USA - 78-0100 |website=45cat.com |date= |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>

"Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast" is a song written by Peter Callander and Geoff Stephens and performed by Wayne Newton. It appeared on Newton's 1972 album, Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast. In the lyrics, the singer is leaving his family after falling out of love with his wife. When his daughter tries to catch up with him, saying "Daddy, don't you walk so fast", it makes him change his mind about ending his marriage.

"Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast" reached No. 3 on the U.S. adult contemporary chart and No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. The song spent one week at No. 1 on the Cashbox chart on August 5, 1972, and three weeks at No. 1 in Australia. It sold over one million copies and was awarded a gold disc by the RIAA in July 1972.

The song was ranked No. 10 on Billboard magazine's Top Hot 100 songs of 1972 and was also ranked No. 7 on the Kent Music Report's 25 songs of 1972.

The track was produced by Wes Farrell and arranged by Mike Melvoin.

sections.heading: Other versions
sections.wikitext:
*[[Daniel Boone (singer)|Daniel Boone]] released the original version of the song as his debut single in [[1971 in music|1971]].  It reached No. 1 in New Zealand and South Africa<ref>{{cite web|title=SA Charts 1965–March 1989|url=http://www.rock.co.za/files/springbok_top_20_(B).html|accessdate=1 September 2018}}</ref> and No. 17 on the [[UK Singles Chart]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicvf.com/song.php?title=Daddy+Don%27t+You+Walk+So+Fast+by+Daniel+Boone&id=10383 |title=Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast (song by Daniel Boone) |website=Musicvf.com |date=1971-08-14 |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>  It was featured on his 1971 album, ''Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.discogs.com/Daniel-Boone-Daddy-Dont-You-Walk-So-Fast/release/2633492 |title=Daniel Boone - Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast (Vinyl, LP) |website=Discogs.com |year=1971 |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>
*[[Ronnie Dove]] recorded the song for his 1973 country album on [[MCA Records]].
* [[:nl:Herman van Keeken|Herman van Keeken]] made a Dutch version of this song in 1971, called "Pappie loop toch niet zo snel", which became a hit in the Netherlands and Flanders.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.originals.be/nl/originals/1207|title = The Originals © by Arnold Rypens - DADDY Don't YOU WALK SO FAST}}</ref>
* [[Roger Johnssson]] wrote a Swedish text and made a Swedish version of this song called "Snälla pappa vänta på mej". This version became a No. 1 hit on the Swedish list [[Svensktoppen]].
* [[Henson Cargill]] released a version as the [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of his [[1972 in music|February 1972]] single, "I Can't Face the Bed Alone".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.45cat.com/record/6150060 |title=Henson Cargill - I Can't Face The Bed Alone / Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast - Mega - USA - 615-0060 |website=45cat.com |date= |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>  It was featured on his 1972 album, ''On the Road''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/on-the-road-mw0000991452 |title=On the Road - Henson Cargill | Songs, Reviews, Credits |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |date= |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>
* [[Frank Ifield]] released a version on [[1972 in music|June 15, 1972]] in [[Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.45cat.com/record/mam9914 |title=Frank Ifield - Daddy, Don't You Walk So Fast / Beautiful Love - MAM - Australia - MAM-9914 |website=45cat.com |date=1972-06-15 |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>
*[[Ace Cannon]] released a version on his 1973 album, ''Baby Dont Get Hooked on Me''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/baby-dont-get-hooked-on-me-mw0000852850 |title=Baby Dont Get Hooked on Me - Ace Cannon | Songs, Reviews, Credits |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |date= |accessdate=2016-06-03}}</ref>

* Henson Cargill released a version as the B-side of his February 1972 single, "I Can't Face the Bed Alone".  It was featured on his 1972 album, On the Road.
* Frank Ifield released a version on June 15, 1972 in Australia.
*Ace Cannon released a version on his 1973 album, Baby Dont Get Hooked on Me.
